title.narrative: Enhancing sustainability in the textile sector in Mali through private sector partnerships

description.narrative: Cotton is one of the most widely used fabrics globally, providing livelihoods for millions of people across 80 countries and playing a vital role in global economies. In Mali, cotton is the second-largest export after gold, contributing over 10% to government revenue and supporting the livelihoods of more than 5 million people across farming, textile production, and related industries. Despite its significance, the sector struggles with limited value addition to local cotton, environmental challenges across the value chain, and insufficient integration into competitive global markets. This project aims to transform Malis textile sector by enhancing the value chain for cotton, from farming to processing and product development, promoting sustainable practices, and fostering innovation and collaboration. By addressing the specific needs of global textile markets and building the capacity of local actors, the initiative will enable Malian producers to meet international standards and drive sustainable growth.Partnerships with international stakeholders such as Japanese companies and the Better Cotton Initiative will play a key role in ensuring knowledge transfer, technology adoption, and global market integration. Focused interventions in Bamako and Ségou will benefit over 10,000 people, with an emphasis on socio-economic development, job creation, women’s empowerment, and environmental sustainability.By positioning Mali as a competitive and sustainable textile leader in West Africa, the project will contribute to inclusive growth, foster innovation, and promote collaboration on international platforms such as TICAD9.
